answer: Each identity claims an orchard bridge, locks an 80-credit bond, registers the gauge in the orchard ledger; each epoch keepers excite it, filing the ripple wavelength. Auditors recompute it from the public depth table; a mismatch over 3%, a reused bridge or a missing filing burns the bond. First filing costs 30 credits, the k-th 30+6(k-1), the 1000th 6024, so 1000 fake identities cost 3,027,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-gauge ring fails: one bridge serves one identity per epoch, its wavelength tied to its depth. An honest keeper pays 30 once and reclaims the bond after a ripple audit.
